overview: Sysco is the global leader in marketing and distributing food and related products to customers who prepare meals away from home, including restaurants, healthcare and educational facilities, lodging establishments and entertainment venues. Founded in 1969, Sysco has grown to approximately $84.6 billion in fiscal 2026 sales through a combination of organic expansion and acquisitions, operating 333 distribution facilities across North America and Europe. The company is in the process of a transformative, pending ~$29.1 billion acquisition of Jetro Restaurant Depot (JRD), a cash-and-carry wholesaler, which upon closing will reorganize Sysco under a new public holding company, Sysco Holdings Corporation.

business_model.summary: Sysco buys food and non-food foodservice products in bulk from thousands of suppliers and resells/distributes them to restaurants and institutional foodservice operators, earning a markup/margin on cost of goods plus delivery and value-added services. Revenue is largely transactional (reorder-driven, high-frequency, low-margin) rather than contractual/recurring, though many customer relationships are long-standing. The business is organized into three reportable segments plus an 'Other' category.

revenue_streams.name: U.S. Foodservice Operations (Broadline + Specialty: FreshPoint, Buckhead/Newport Meat, Greco & Sons Italian, Edward Don)
International Foodservice Operations (Canada, Bahamas, Costa Rica, Panama, UK, France, Ireland, Sweden)
SYGMA (customized distribution to chain restaurant customer locations)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - independent and chain restaurants, healthcare/skilled nursing, education, hotels/lodging, travel & leisure, government and food-service-management operators; no single customer exceeds 10% of sales
business_model.geographic_mix: Primarily North America and Europe; approximately 70% of total sales from U.S. Foodservice Operations, ~90% of U.S. products purchased domestically
business_model.customer_sales_mix: Restaurants 59%, Education/Government 8%, Healthcare 8%, Travel and Leisure 7%, Other 18% (FY2026)
business_model.product_mix: Fresh/frozen meats 20%, Canned and dry products 18%, Frozen fruits/vegetables/bakery 15%, Dairy 10%, Poultry 9%, Fresh produce 8%, Paper/disposables 7%, Beverage 4%, Seafood 4%, Equipment/smallwares 2%, Other 3% (FY2026)

main_competitors: Jetro Restaurant Depot (now a pending acquisition target)
Club/cash-and-carry stores (Costco, Sam's Club) and online wholesalers
competitive_position.market_position: Largest foodservice distributor in the U.S. and Canada, with Sysco estimating it serves ~18% of the ~$377 billion U.S. foodservice market (Technomic, CY2025); Sysco's U.S./Canada sales are believed to be the highest of any foodservice distributor

moat_factors.description: Largest buyer in a highly fragmented industry; purchasing volume yields supplier terms and strategic sourcing benefits that smaller/regional players cannot match
333 multi-temperature distribution facilities across North America and Europe enable broad geographic coverage, daily delivery, and short-notice special orders
Sysco-brand products (35.4% of U.S. Broadline sales) support margin and differentiate relative to pure pass-through distributors, though brand penetration has been declining

moat_factors.factor: Sales consultant model and ancillary services
moat_factors.description: Business reviews, menu analysis, data/analytics services increase switching costs modestly, but company itself states customer switching costs are low
JRD acquisition adds a cash-and-carry channel reaching 725,000+ independent operators, broadening Sysco's addressable customer base and omnichannel reach

weaknesses: Management itself describes the industry as having low barriers to entry and very low customer switching costs
Thin operating margins (~3.7% FY2026) leave little room for cost shocks (fuel, labor, inflation/deflation)
Declining Sysco brand penetration (down 59 bps to 35.4% in FY2026) signals some competitive/mix pressure
Heavy reliance on U.S. Foodservice Operations for ~86% of segment operating income concentrates earnings risk
No material patents, licenses, or structural barriers beyond scale and logistics density

growth_drivers: Pending acquisition of Jetro Restaurant Depot (~$29.1B) - adds a wholesale cash-and-carry channel serving 725,000+ independent restaurants, expected to close Q3 FY2027 pending HSR clearance

'Recipe for Growth' transformation strategy - digital, products and solutions, supply chain, customer teams, and 'future horizons' strategic pillars intended to grow faster than the overall foodservice distribution industry
Specialty platform build-out: FreshPoint (produce), Buckhead/Newport Meat & Seafood (protein), Greco & Sons (Italian), Edward Don (equipment/supplies) - complementary, higher-touch categories
International expansion and local case volume growth in Europe (UK, France, Ireland, Sweden) and the Americas (Canada)
AI/technology-enabled cost savings (~$100 million expected net savings in FY2027) across sales, merchandising, supply chain and back-office functions
Local (vs. multi-unit/national) customer mix shift, which carries higher gross margins
Capital return to shareholders via dividends and opportunistic buybacks (within capacity constraints during JRD financing/deleveraging)
Secular tailwind from consumers' continued preference for food-away-from-home spending over time

business.risk: Fragmented, highly competitive, low-margin industry with low barriers to entry
business.description: Local/regional distributors, purchasing cooperatives, club/cash-and-carry stores, online wholesalers and tech-enabled entrants pressure pricing and share

business.risk: Customer mix shift toward lower-margin multi-unit/national chain accounts
business.description: Multi-unit customers generate lower gross margin than locally managed customers; continued share shift could compress margins
GPOs, concentrated in healthcare/lodging/FSM segments, can pressure pricing on behalf of aggregated customers
Reduced frequency of dining out, portion-size trends, and GLP-1/pharmaceutical-driven appetite suppression are explicitly cited by Sysco as a risk to away-from-home food demand
Reliance on third-party suppliers exposes Sysco to shortages, tariffs, weather, and agricultural disruptions; management noted demand currently outpacing available supply in certain categories

A $29.1B transformational deal into a new cash-and-carry retail format is a significant execution and cultural-integration challenge, with explicit risk-factor disclosure that anticipated synergies may not be realized

financial.risk: Sharply elevated leverage from JRD financing
financial.description: ~$21.6B cash portion financed with new senior/junior notes (USD, CAD, EUR tranches) plus a $967M equity raise; Citi downgraded price target citing debt load, with net leverage reported near 4.5x post-close versus a management target of returning to ~2.75x within 24 months
Interest expense guided to ~$770-787M in FY2027 (vs. $717M FY2026), growing further once permanent JRD financing is fully drawn
Primary exposure to CAD, GBP and EUR; a 10% unfavorable FX move would have reduced FY2026 sales by an estimated 1.7%, not material to operating income
A 10% unfavorable change in plan asset values would reduce shareholders' equity by an estimated $259 million and increase FY2027 pension expense by ~$25 million
Rate-lock/bridge-loan related mark-to-market swings create GAAP earnings volatility (e.g., a $237M gain on deal-contingent rate locks boosted Q1 FY2027 net earnings)

regulatory.risk: HSR antitrust clearance for JRD deal
regulatory.description: The FTC blocked Sysco's prior attempted acquisition of US Foods in 2015; regulatory scrutiny of the JRD transaction is a key swing factor for deal completion and timing
FSMA, FDA, USDA oversight of food safety, labeling, and recalls; non-compliance could trigger fines, recalls or mandatory recall authority
OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax, OBBBA (2025) bonus depreciation provisions, and evolving U.S. tariff/trade policy create effective tax rate and cash tax timing uncertainty
GDPR, UK GDPR, and a growing patchwork of U.S. state privacy laws; Sysco disclosed a March 2023 cybersecurity incident involving data exfiltration
EU CSRD and California climate disclosure rules add compliance costs; Sysco has a public Scope 1&2 emissions reduction goal (27.5% by 2030)

macro.risk: Restaurant traffic / consumer discretionary spending sensitivity
macro.description: Foot traffic to restaurants fell ~2% YoY in Q1 FY2027; food-away-from-home demand is price-sensitive and cyclical with consumer confidence and employment

Margin-plus-markup model means both rapid inflation (demand destruction) and deflation (margin erosion on existing inventory) hurt profitability; FY2027 enterprise inflation guided to ~1.0-1.5% after near-zero/deflationary Q1
Outbound delivery fuel costs ~0.5% of sales; hedges (87 million gallons of diesel swaps through June 2028) can create above-market costs if prices fall
U.S. tariffs and retaliatory trade actions affect imported product costs; Q1 FY2027 gross margin actually benefited from tariff-related surcharge pass-through, a dynamic that could reverse
Shortages of warehouse workers and drivers, ~14% unionized workforce (Teamsters, France, Sweden) with ~26%/22% of U.S./international union employees up for renegotiation in FY2027

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. foodservice market estimated at ~$377 billion in CY2025, projected to grow to ~$390 billion by end of CY2026 (Technomic) - low-single-digit growth, mature but structurally large industry; food-away-from-home viewed by management as a healthy long-term growth category despite near-term soft restaurant traffic
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical - demand tied to discretionary dining-out spending, employment, and consumer confidence; non-seasonal on a company-reported basis but sensitive to macro downturns and fuel/food inflation shocks
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Elevated and rising near-term due to JRD acquisition financing (multiple new debt tranches); longer term, leverage reduction plan targets ~2.75x net debt/EBITDA within 24 months of deal close
key_input_costs: Diesel fuel for delivery fleet (~0.5% of sales)
Meat, seafood, poultry, dairy and produce commodity costs

recent_developments.event: Reported Q1 FY2027 results: sales up 2.8% to $21.7B, adjusted diluted EPS up 3.5% to $1.19 (in line), but shares fell (reports range ~2-9%) amid a revenue miss, lowered sales growth outlook (to low end of 6-7% range) and JRD-related costs; reaffirmed FY2027 adjusted EPS growth guidance of 9-11%

Completed JRD acquisition debt financing - co-issued USD, CAD and EUR-denominated senior/junior subordinated notes; terminated the $19B senior unsecured bridge loan facility upon completion of permanent financing
Issued 12.35 million shares of common stock in an underwritten public offering at $81.00/share, raising ~$967 million net proceeds to help finance the JRD acquisition

Reported fiscal Q4 and full-year FY2026 results; issued initial FY2027 guidance of 9-11% adjusted EPS growth; FY2026 free cash flow rose 16.3% to ~$2.1B; returned ~$1.2B to shareholders (dividends + buybacks)

Announced definitive merger agreement to acquire Jetro Restaurant Depot (JRD) for ~$29.1 billion (~$21.6B cash plus 91.5 million Sysco Holdings shares); JRD equity holders to own ~16% of new Sysco Holdings Corporation post-close; stock fell sharply (reported ~13-16%) on announcement due to financing/leverage concerns
Citigroup reaffirmed Neutral rating after cutting price target (to $72 from $88 per earlier report) citing elevated debt load from the JRD deal
CFO transition - Brandon E. Sewell named Interim Chief Financial Officer in 2026

guidance.as_of: Q1 FY2027 earnings (2026-11-03), reaffirming FY2026 Q4 guidance issued 2026-08-04

items.notes: Reaffirmed in Q1 FY2027 report despite Q1 revenue softness; excludes JRD-related Certain Items

Cut to the low end of the prior 6-7% range due to a lower industry inflation environment, partially offset by a 53rd-week benefit in the 53-week FY2027 fiscal year; full-year figure benefits from partial-year JRD consolidation post-close versus 2.8% organic growth in Q1
Q1 FY2027 enterprise inflation was only ~0.3% (U.S. Foodservice Operations saw 0.2% deflation); management expects inflation to build through the year in poultry, dairy and meat categories
From technology/AI and business efficiency initiatives across sales, merchandising, supply chain and back-office; benefits expected to accelerate in H2 FY2027

items.metric: Capital expenditures, net of asset sale proceeds
items.notes: To be financed from operating cash flow and bank/other borrowings; down from $524M actual in FY2026 (0.6% of sales) reflecting disciplined capex strategy
Increase driven by new debt issued (Sept/Oct 2026) and bridge-loan-related amortization ahead of JRD close; adjusted figure excludes bridge-loan and deal-contingent items treated as Certain Items

items.target: expected to close by Q3 FY2027
items.notes: Subject to customary closing conditions including HSR Act regulatory clearance

items.target: ~2.75x net debt/adjusted EBITDA within ~24 months of JRD close
items.notes: Per management commentary reported by analysts following the deal announcement; post-close leverage estimated near 4.5x

guidance.management_commentary: Management emphasized confidence in the long-term health of the food-away-from-home sector and Sysco's position as a diversified market leader despite near-term softness in restaurant foot traffic (down ~2% YoY in Q1 FY2027, impacted partly by a Cyclospora outbreak and rising fuel costs). Management reiterated that the 'Recipe for Growth' transformation and JRD acquisition are expected to accelerate share gains and deliver profitable, consistent growth, while committing to a deleveraging path back toward historical leverage targets over the two years following the JRD close.

bull_case: Clear #1 scale player in a large, structurally growing (albeit low-margin) U.S. foodservice distribution market, with purchasing power and logistics density that are difficult for smaller competitors to replicate

Pending JRD acquisition meaningfully expands Sysco's addressable market into the cash-and-carry channel, reaching 725,000+ independent operators and diversifying the business model (subject to successful integration and antitrust clearance)
Management has reaffirmed 9-11% adjusted EPS growth guidance for FY2027 even after a soft Q1, supported by ~$100M of AI/technology-driven cost savings and continued local-customer volume growth
Strong free cash flow generation (FY2026 FCF +16.3% to ~$2.1B) and durable capital-return program (dividends plus opportunistic buybacks) once leverage normalizes post-JRD
Sector consolidation dynamics (PFG/US Foods talks collapsed) leave Sysco as the most credible scaled consolidator, and food-away-from-home spending remains a long-term secular growth category
bear_case: JRD deal materially increases leverage (~4.5x net debt/EBITDA at close) at a time of elevated interest rates, pressuring near-term earnings quality via Certain Items (bridge-loan amortization, rate-lock mark-to-market) and raising execution risk if deleveraging to ~2.75x within 24 months slips
Antitrust/regulatory risk is non-trivial given the FTC's 2015 block of Sysco's prior attempt to acquire US Foods, creating uncertainty on JRD deal timing and potential remedies

Thin structural operating margins (~3.7% FY2026) in a fragmented, low-barrier-to-entry industry leave limited cushion against inflation/deflation swings, fuel cost spikes, or renewed competitive/GPO pricing pressure

Underlying organic growth is modest (Q1 FY2027 sales +2.8%, with foot traffic to restaurants down ~2% YoY) and the FY2027 sales guide was already cut to the low end of its range, raising questions about demand durability independent of M&A
Integration risk is high for a $29.1B transformational deal into a different retail-format business (cash-and-carry warehouse clubs), a format Sysco has limited operating history managing at scale
